method: two independent judges, fresh (told not to read SCORECARD or earlier rejudge files before scoring; each disclosed seeing the README's quoted earlier total once): A execution / measurement lens (ran the tests, the jury chain, dry runs warm / cold / offline, base vs reviewed image, the six recordings, set O and six ride files), B safety sceptic / code and evidence auditor (no heavy runs); combined = per-criterion mean rounded down to 0.5

criteria.name: Functionality (detection, misses, false alarms, unseen data)
reasons: Real obstacle (doubleT_obstacle, 201 frames, own matcher vs labels/doubleT_obstacle.json): person STOP in 61/61 in-envelope frames, object on rail in 162/185 frames where it has points; STOP in 190/201 frames from frame 8 (+0.8 s); STOP distances 55.51-56.56 m, max error vs labels 0.44 m (median 0.03 m). Identical in the offline detector, 13 dry runs (reviewed + base image, warm/cold, network none), the README jury chain and play_bag.sh.
Clear bag roundT_doubleT: 0 STOP frames of 252 in the offline run and in 7 ROS runs.

Four other empty organizer recordings streamed and run by me (doubleT_platform, roundT_pressureGate_roundT, roundT_squareT_pressureGate_squareT, squareT_platform_squareT_switch) + roundT_doubleT = 2,287 frames: 7 false STOP episodes / 23 STOP frames (1.0 % of frames); 5 of the 7 in squareT_platform_squareT_switch at 83-148 m, 1 platform at 39 m, 1 pressure gate at 54.5 m. Two straight ride segments (new_data 46-48, 68-70, 306 frames): 0 STOP.

Organizers' synthetic objects (cloud_with_fake_obj, 1,510 frames, played through the node, 1510/1510 processed): all 8 in-envelope objects get a STOP, but only 424 of 801 in-envelope object-frames (53 %); STOP on the outside 2x2 m box in 9 frames (6 of them at 132-142 m); 0 STOP in empty background frames apart from 6 frames 1.4-5.4 m right after an object passes the sensor.

Misses: a deterministic GO at frame 111 and CAUTION at frames 117/197 while the object on the rail is visible (about 20 points) at 56 m; small objects are STOPped late (see 8.2); set F 0.5 m box on the bed found in only 2 of 4 approaches.
missing: No held-out real obstacle data: every recording I could use was also seen by the team (set O explicitly tuned on), so 'unseen data' performance is not demonstrated
Recall per frame on organizer-style objects is only ~53 %; the edge and small objects are missed until 28-56 m
Remove the single-frame GO/CAUTION drop-outs on a persistent in-envelope object

criteria.name: Detection range
reasons: Own set F runs (scripts/far_range_eval.py, anchored placement, ride segments 46-48 and 68-70, seeds 0 and 1, 4 approaches per kind from 220 m, no speed): person detected 4/4, first confirmed 144-180 m, >=90 % held from 85-158 m; recall 50-100 m 82/100, 100-150 m 65/94, 150-200 m 4/86. 1 m crate: first 79-112 m, held from 85-122 m. 3 cm hanging cable: first 46-88 m, held from 23-49 m. 0.5 m box on the bed: 2/4, first 42-64 m.

Organizers' objects (node path, own matcher): 2x2 m box centre STOP from 98.2 m (its first appearance, 98.7 m), 2x2 m box at the envelope top from 111.4 m (56 of 124 frames), plank across the rails 89.0 m, 0.3 m cubes 48.0 m (on rail) and 55.8 m (centre), edge cube 35.0 m, edge 2x2 m box 28.2 m, 5 cm hanging object 30.1 m.
Real obstacle only at 55-57 m (stationary recording) - STOP there from +0.8 s.

By the organizers' scale (100 m good, 200 very good, 300 excellent): large objects and a person reach the 'good' band (roughly 100-150 m first, 85-120 m sustained); the organizers' minimum-size objects stay below 60 m, and the sensor returns nothing beyond ~210 m.
missing: Reliable STOP of 0.3-0.5 m objects beyond 60-100 m
Edge-of-envelope objects beyond ~35 m
Range numbers on data not used for tuning

criteria.name: Speed
reasons: 4 vCPU Xeon 2.1 GHz, reviewed image, 5 warm dry runs at 360 deg: every one of the 201 frames processed, 0 recording messages unprocessed after settle, 10.1 fps; decode+detect p95 65-82 ms (median 75); end-to-end (freshness.source_age_s, valid results) median 71-78 ms, p95 87-111 ms (median 102), max 146-242 ms; node CPU 0.7-0.8 cores, peak RSS 340-476 MB. Cold page cache: e2e p95 118 ms.

120 deg (roundT_doubleT, same format as most recordings): decode+detect p95 46-58 ms, e2e p95 54-64 ms (cold 64 ms), 10.1 fps, 0.4-0.5 cores, RSS ~130 MB; set O through the node: e2e p95 50 ms, 0 drops over 1,510 frames.
Detector alone (resense bench, native kernels, one core): mean 27.4 / p95 41.6 ms at 360 deg, 23.8 / 33.5 ms at 120 deg; offline node path (bench_node_path): decode+detect p95 62.3 / 45.6 ms.

Before/after of this pass (resense:base vs resense:ci, 5 alternating pairs each): e2e p95 median 113 -> 102 ms, e2e median 82 -> 73 ms, current results 166 -> 179 of 201; decode+detect p95 75 -> 75 ms (no change). Fast input path byte-identical on 453/453 frames (their script in the image and my own check with the rosbags deserializer).
CI runner (806b6c4, cold): 360 deg e2e p95 60 ms, 120 deg 37 ms - the faster stand should do better than this sandbox.
missing: At 360 deg the p95 end-to-end is at the 100 ms frame period on this hardware, and the first 1.5-4 s of a 360 deg playback yield no current result
No measurement on an i7-9700E-class machine

criteria.name: Generalization
reasons: The method models the tunnel (per-frame rail/bed/axis fit, curvature from walls, organizer envelope 2.1 x 3.0 m) and needs no object classes or map - what spec 8.4 asks for; mount auto-calibration handled both mounts (360 deg 'livox' and 120 deg 'hesai' recordings) and the organizers' synthetic recording without configuration changes.

I ran it on all 6 original recordings, the organizers' set O and 6 ride split files: behaviour is stable (0 false STOP on the straight ride segments and 2 of 5 empty bags), with false STOPs concentrated on the platform/switch recording (5 episodes at 83-148 m); STOP still fires on the organizers' objects placed at the edge/top of the envelope.

Limits: all this data was available to the team and many rules (374-line config) and a learned track opinion were tuned on it; set F is the team's own synthetic generator; the only real obstacle is one stationary scene at 55 m; I could not test data the team never saw.
missing: A held-out evaluation on genuinely unseen tunnels / new obstacle recordings
Fewer hand-tuned rules or evidence that they transfer (e.g. leave-one-recording-out)

criteria.name: Technical quality
reasons: pytest on host 748 passed / 1 deselected (no data cache), in the reviewed image 740 passed; ruff clean; detector_freeze verify PASS (31 files); sync_params --check in sync; CI run 36397511351 on 806b6c4: checks, pytest, docker, offline-build all green.

Clear package structure (resense/ stages per module, C++ kernels with numpy fallback, ROS node separate); acceptance scripts (dry_run.sh, check_dry_run.py, play_bag.sh, check_fast_input.py, far_range_eval.py) ran for me as documented and reproduced the headline detection numbers.
Moderate resources (CPU-only, <1 core, 0.13-0.48 GB RSS).
Minus: the documentation is very large and hard to navigate (README 625 lines with dated history, EXPERIMENTS 3,726 lines), and some numbers of this pass are overstated (see claims list).
missing: A short, current, single-source results page; stale dated numbers moved out of README
Corrected speed-claim table and docstrings

criteria.name: Ease of launch
reasons: README 'Кратко для жюри' chain done by hand: node container (--net=host), player from another container as uid 1000 with --read-ahead-queue-size 10, topic echo: decision FAULT -> STOP 55.5-56.6 m on doubleT_obstacle, GO/CAUTION and no STOP on roundT_doubleT.

criteria.name: Team approach

criteria.name: Functionality (working solution)
reasons: Works end to end in Docker/ROS 2: CI run 36397511351 (806b6c4) plays both original bags cold through the node and passes; I recomputed the node's per-frame status captures myself.

Real obstacle (doubleT_obstacle, stationary train): the crossing person gets a STOP on 61 of 61 in-envelope frames, from frame 8 (the first frame inside the envelope), distance error <= 0.03 m against the labels. Recomputed from 4 node captures (ab/new_obst_1/2, cold_local, base).

Object on the rail (0.45 x 0.6 x 0.27 m, 56 m): on the product path (node, raw bag) 150 of 185 labelled visible frames are matched by a STOP detection. After frame 75 the decision is STOP on 123 of 126 frames: GO at frame 111 (11.1 s), CAUTION at frames 117 and 197. This is deterministic in all 5 captures of the 27.09 detector, including CI run 36319767736. The docs claim 125/126, taken from the offline replay on a quantised cache.
Clear 120-degree recording roundT_doubleT through the node: 0 STOP frames in 5 captures. But CAUTION is on 170 of 252 frames (67 %) and GO on only 81, so CAUTION carries little information.

False alarms I verified per frame (P3d detector of 26.09, freeze_2026-09-26/gate_frames): ride 45 events, 183 alarm frames and 38 STOP episodes in 20 min / 13 km (3.5 per km, about one false STOP episode every 32 s of riding; 93 of 183 alarm frames within 50 m); five empty bags 13 events / 58 frames / 16 episodes. All of these match the team's P3d figures exactly, so their counting is honest.

The current detector's improved figures (ride 32 in-sample / 37 cross-fitted, five empty bags 11) exist only as aggregates (regression_gate_2026-09-27_quality.json, opinion_crossfit_2x_margin.json). The per-frame outputs are not committed, so I give them no credit.

Missed obstacles on the organizers' own synthetic objects (P3d, recomputed): STOP on 384 of 801 in-envelope object-frames (48 %). The edge objects only get a STOP at 5-10 m. On the novel placements, the only per-frame output of the current detector (novel_results.json.gz, recomputed): 723 of 2458 visible frames (29 %), 45 of 72 cases. The 2 x 2 m box at the envelope top gets a STOP in only 5 of 18 cases; 13 of those cases come within 30 m and never get one. The 5 cm hanging object gets a STOP in 9 of 18 cases.
missing: Commit the per-frame outputs of the sealed 27.09 detector on the ride, the five empty bags and set O, so that 32/37 events and 411/801 can be recomputed.
Explain or fix the GO at doubleT_obstacle frame 111 on the node path (two consecutive misses drop a confirmed low track); consider a longer hold for a confirmed static in-envelope track.
Bring false STOP episodes on the ride down substantially: 31-38 episodes in 20 min is not operable.
Make CAUTION rarer or split it (infrastructure vs degraded monitoring) so that it keeps a meaning.

criteria.name: Detection range
reasons: Real data: the only real obstacles are at 55.5-56.6 m in front of a standing train (verified). No real approach from far away exists in the data.

Organizers' synthetic objects (set O, P3d per-frame output, recomputed): 2 x 2 m box STOP from 98.0 m (208 of 213 frames); box at the envelope top from 101.3 m (51 of 124); plank across the rails 82.2 m; 0.3 m cubes 42.7-52.5 m; 5 cm hanging object 30.1 m; edge cube 5.2 m and edge box 10.3 m. By the organizers' scale that is 'good' (about 100 m) only for large objects; small ones reach about 50 m.
Current-detector gains (box at the top 111 m, plank 87 m, edge cube 35 m) and the team's own synthetic person at 151 m are aggregate-only: no credit.
The sensor limit is real. Sampled frames reach 199-209 m at most (verified with rosbags on 4 frames), so 300 m is impossible with this LiDAR. The team says so honestly.
By the team's own pitch, braking from 80 km/h needs about 200 m, while the verified confident range is about 100 m (large objects) and about 50 m (small ones).
missing: Commit per-frame evidence for the current detector's set O and set F range figures.
Show far-range recall with an in-sample/held-out split, for example the set O shapes placed at new offsets out to 150 m on the ride.

criteria.name: Speed
reasons: Recomputed from the committed raw captures (docs/evidence/node_input_2026-09-28): end-to-end (player publication -> result, over current results) at 360 degrees, base 120.2 / 127.4 ms p95 -> new 93.0 / 97.1 ms, cold 114.4 ms. At 120 degrees: base 76.0 / 67.9 -> new 60.8 / 56.8, cold 59.0. Node CPU 0.71 / 0.73 cores (360) and 0.45-0.47 (120); peak RSS 408-476 MB. Every number matches the claims.

The CI runner's cold baseline of 126.3 / 49.3 ms (run 36319767736) recomputed exactly. The new CI run 36397511351 (806b6c4) measures 60 / 37 ms p95 end to end, 45 / 33 ms decode+detect and 10 fps, so the claims are conservative.
Per stage (recomputed): decode median 19.3 ms (360) / 7.8-8.0 ms (120); detect median 32.6-33.5 / 27.5-28.4 ms.

Caveats: the p95 covers current results only (179-182 of 201 frames at 360 degrees; over all frames p95 is 243-455 ms because of the start-up burst). The sandbox 360-degree p95 sits just under the 100 ms period. The team's own worst dense stretch of the ride is 111 ms p95 on one core. The executor is single-threaded Python.

Small overstatements: the node docstring, fastcloud.py and the launch help say rclpy conversion costs '~21 ms'; the team's own fast_input.json gives 12.5 ms median (CI: 7.0). fastcloud.py says the decode takes '14 ms instead of 20'; measured 18.1 vs 19.2 ms on the sandbox, and on CI the fast decode is slower (9.30 vs 8.82 ms).
missing: Measure on 8 cores or state the headroom there.
Quote the all-frame p95 next to the current-results p95.
Fix the '~21 ms' and '14 vs 20 ms' statements.

criteria.name: Generalization
reasons: The concept fits the brief: no map, the track bed, rails, axis and curvature re-estimated in every frame, the mount self-calibrated, anomaly detection in the envelope without object classes.

In practice the detector is a very large hand-tuned rule system: 332 configuration keys in configs/default.yaml, about 15 of them dead or opt-in. There are many shape demotions (column, floating, elevated, wall_face, edge, beyond_axis, beyond_height_ref) plus keep/escalation/hold rules, most sized on the same 7 recordings and set O. Examples: column_hold sized on the roundT_doubleT column; the edge cube's 35 m depends on floating_free_max_dy 1.2, 'in a window bracketed by two set O objects'.

The learned opinion uses ride tracks as negatives (205 rows) and synthetic insertions as positives (2646 rows / 102 sequences). The per-fold thresholds range from 0.0061 to 0.0327. Only the opinion is cross-fitted (37 vs 32 events); every other rule stays in-sample.

The only held-out-like test (novel placements of seen shapes on seen backgrounds, per-frame output of the current detector) gives 29 % of frames and 45 of 72 cases; the box at the envelope top gets 5 of 18 cases and the hanging object 9 of 18.

The ground truth is produced by the team's own pipeline: doubleT_obstacle labels come from DBSCAN plus estimate_track, and set O labels are 'mount-calibrated by the shipped detector'. The headline offline numbers run on a 1 cm-quantised cache with bag receive stamps, which behaves differently from the node on the raw bag (frame 111).
missing: A genuinely held-out evaluation (leave-one-recording-out for every rule, not only the opinion).
Cut the parameter surface and remove dead options.
Recall on novel placements across the full envelope (top, edges, hanging) with the causes fixed.

criteria.name: Technical quality
reasons: Clear architecture (core library, ROS node, native kernels with a numpy fallback). There are 521 test functions, and CI in two stages covers lint, the detector seal, pytest plus web tests, and the jury path in Docker: a uid-1000 player, stock Fast DDS, an offline rebuild, the original bags cold and the fast-input identity check.

The new input path is correct on the covered layouts. tests/test_fastcloud.py passes (11) and tests/test_node.py passes (51). My own probes confirm big-endian CDR encapsulation is parsed correctly, XCDR2 and malformed input raise ValueError and fall back, and the fast parse is identical to an independent deserializer (rosbags) on 6 real messages of both bags. CI reports 453/453 identical frames.

Gaps in the new path: an exception from the rclpy fallback in as_cloud() is not caught in on_cloud(), so it would escape executor.spin() and stop the node; the 'never dies on a bad frame' promise does not cover it. height > 1 with row padding (row_step > width*point_step) is decoded wrongly by both paths (pre-existing). An unknown datatype on an unused field raises KeyError, which means FAULT on every frame. None of these, nor big-endian CDR, is covered by a test; the raw executor path is covered only by stubs in the unit tests, though CI exercises the real one.

Readability suffers: detector.py has 775 lines of interacting rules and tracking.py 624. YAML parameters carry paragraph-long inline histories, and there are about 13 k lines of documentation (EXPERIMENTS.md alone is 3726 lines). 'Quickly understand the solution' is hard.
The per-frame outputs of the sealed detector are not committed (aggregates only), so the headline numbers cannot be reproduced without re-running.

criteria.name: Ease of launch
reasons: docker load of a CI-built offline archive, then docker run, then ros2 bag play. There is a one-command scripts/play_bag.sh; CI job docker step 'the one-command wrapper' was green on 806b6c4. The node auto-discovers either topic/frame pair, and the readiness wait replaces fixed sleeps.

Several non-obvious knobs are needed: --net=host is mandatory; freshness_mode:=replay is required for recordings (the default 'live' turns every frame of a historical bag into FAULT/STOP, never GO); --read-ahead-queue-size 10 is recommended because the default read-ahead failed freshness cold; sysctl rmem_max is needed for a CycloneDDS player.
docker build on the stand is impossible (no internet, per the organizers). The archive route is the right answer but adds a step.
The output needs explaining: four states, with CAUTION on 67 % of clear frames.
Minor: in play_bag.sh the readiness loop 'docker logs | grep -q' runs under set -o pipefail, so a SIGPIPE could make a found line read as not found (low risk with small logs).
missing: Make replay the automatic choice when stamps are far from UTC (or detect it and warn).
Build the read-ahead limit into the documented player command in every place.
Reduce the required flags.

criteria.name: Team approach
reasons: The process is unusually systematic: pre-registered candidates, a regression gate with the ride, ablations (one mechanism off at a time), cross-fitting of the learned opinion, negative results kept as flags with numbers (EXPERIMENTS 'tried, not shipped', DECISIONS), and repeated independent reviews that found and fixed safety regressions.

The P3d numbers I recomputed (ride 45 / 183 / 38, five empty bags 13 / 58 / 16, set O 384 / 801 and 6 outside-box frames) match the team's records exactly, which supports the integrity of their bookkeeping.

However, the process mostly iterates micro-rules against the same recordings. DECISIONS.md is stale ('Last verified 26.09', no row for the 27.09 opinion and reference decisions), and the documentation volume buries the trade-offs.

claims_found_wrong_or_overstated: Object on the rail '125 of the 126 frames after the person leaves it' (README, video, deck): this comes from the offline replay on a quantised cache with receive stamps. On the product path (node on the original bag) the 27.09 detector gives STOP on 123/126, with a GO at frame 111 (11.1 s) and CAUTION at frames 117 and 197, reproducibly (5 captures incl. CI 36319767736). The GO is not documented anywhere I found; the node_input README only says 'Detections unchanged'.

The opinion delays a STOP 'by at most 10 frames (~1 s)' / 'не больше чем на 1 с за жизнь трека': the budget counts processed frames (doubt_extra_hits 10, sticky), so it is 2 s at 5 Hz and up to 3 s during a 0.3 s catch-up.

rclpy conversion 'about 21 ms per 24 MB cloud' (detector_node.py docstring, fastcloud.py, launch help): the team's own fast_input.json has 12.5 ms median / 32 ms p95 (sandbox) and CI 7.0 / 30 ms. EXPERIMENTS/CHANGELOG use 12.5, so the docs contradict each other.

fastcloud.py: the one-gather decode '14 ms instead of 20 ms per 360-degree cloud, 5 instead of 8': sequential measurement 18.1 vs 19.2 ms and 5.8 vs 7.2 ms; on the CI runner the fast decode is slower (9.30 vs 8.82 ms, 3.48 vs 3.27 ms).

End-to-end 'p95 93-97 ms at 360 degrees' is over current (valid) results only, which excludes the start-up. Over all frames the p95 is 243-455 ms. For the baseline only 103-122 of 201 frames were current, so before/after compare different subsets (the direction holds, and CI confirms it).

The current detector's headline quality numbers (ride 32 in-sample / 37 held-out events, five empty 11, set O 411/801, edge cube 35 m, box 111 m, person 151 m) cannot be verified: no per-frame output is committed, only aggregates.
'Ground truth' is not independent: the doubleT_obstacle labels come from the team's DBSCAN plus estimate_track axis, and set O is 'mount-calibrated by the shipped detector'.
DECISIONS.md 'Last verified 2026-09-26' leaves out the 27.09 decisions; the README header says 'Last verified 2026-09-27' although the table carries 28.09 node numbers.
The node docstring says 'The node never dies on a bad frame', but an exception in the raw-bytes fallback (deserialize_message) raised in on_cloud() is not caught.
safety_concerns: A confirmed real obstacle can flip to GO: on doubleT_obstacle the 0.27 m object on the rail at 56 m gets GO at frame 111 because the low track misses 2 frames in a row (hold_misses 1), with fresh input and valid freshness. It reproduces on every full node capture of the current detector.

The learned opinion (a gradient-boosted tree model trained on synthetic positives and ride negatives) withholds a first STOP beyond 25 m for up to 10 processed frames, sticky to the opinion at onset: 1 s at 10 Hz is about 20 m at 72 km/h, and more at lower processed rates. It is exempt only for bodies at least 1 m tall within 40 m.

Many demotion rules (column, floating, elevated, edge, beyond_axis, beyond_height_ref, column_hold, approach_block, rail_start_within) turn in-envelope objects into CAUTION. CAUTION is on 41-67 % of clear frames, so in practice a demoted real object is hidden in noise. Novel placements show the 2 x 2 m box at the envelope top missed in 13 of 18 cases, even inside 30 m.
False STOPs: 38 STOP episodes in 20 minutes on the ride (P3d, verified); the claimed 31-34 for the current detector is still more than one false emergency brake per minute.

The freshness contract is sound as implemented: GO needs valid freshness; STOP is latched through FAULT and cleared only by a fresh valid non-STOP result; the watchdog gives FAULT after 0.5 s. But while the single-threaded executor is busy the watchdog cannot run, so the last published GO stays on the topic until the next frame. The README correctly tells consumers to apply their own timer.
rail_start_within 4 m withholds a low track that was never seen beyond 4 m (a standing train at start-up); this is documented.
